130.0.0.en: Out of the depths have I cried unto You, O LORD.

130.0.1.en: 1- After the one ascending to the temple has passed through the suffering of many pains during the ascent, as appears from the previous psalms, he reaches the point of crying out to God from the depths of his heart. A cry of the heart may not need a cry of the lips, like the cry of Abel's blood from the ground (Gen 4:10), and the heartfelt cry of Moses before the Red Sea (Ex 14:15), and the cry of the silent one, the mother of Samuel (1 Sam 1:13). This shows two things:

130.0.2.en: a- The extent of his suffering from lusts, or problems, or afflictions.

130.0.3.en: b- The extent of his faith in God, who is able to rescue him.

130.0.4.en: 2- The depths may be the depths of God, that is, the spiritual man has reached the depths of God and from there cries out to Him; for whoever enters into the depths, his longings toward God increase, and his faith in Him and his hope in Him.

130.0.5.en: 3- These words may be a prophecy about Christ, who went down to the depths of Hades before the Cross, and cried out to the Father, declaring the accomplishment of the redemption by which Adam and his children ascend from Hades to Paradise.

130.1.0.en: Lord, hear my voice; let Your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.

130.1.1.en: 1- David asks God to hear his voice and to open His ears to his supplications. This shows two things:

130.1.2.en: a- His humility and his great need of God.

130.1.3.en: b- His faith in the power of God, who is able to rescue him from all his troubles.

130.2.0.en: If You, LORD, should mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand? For there is forgiveness with You. That

130.2.2.en: 1- David shows the justice of God and the sin of man, for there is no man without sin, and therefore no one can stand before God to be judged or to defend himself; because all have gone astray and become corrupt, there is none who does good (Ps 14:3).

130.2.3.en: 2- The just God is also the merciful One who forgives. Forgiveness comes from the Son who is with the Father, for it is He who will redeem humanity, and with this hope the believing penitent can stand before God, who is just and merciful at the same time.

130.2.4.en: 3- If a person receives forgiveness, he thanks God and does not become negligent, but remains holding fast to the fear of the just God, or else he loses forgiveness, that is, he works out his salvation with fear and trembling (Heb 2:3).

130.2.5.en: However many afflictions meet you, take refuge in God and cry out to Him, for He awaits you in His love. And however great your sins, He will forgive them for you. But hold fast to His commandments and His fear, and you will live in repentance and in peace all your days.

130.3.0.en: I waited for You, O LORD; my soul waits, and in His word do I hope.

130.3.1.en: 1- In his affliction David looked to God, and was not occupied with his sins or his weakness, or the difficulty of the affliction, but in faith he waited for God, that is, he was not disturbed by the delay of God's answer.

130.3.2.en: 2- David concentrated on waiting for the Lord, and confirmed this by repeating the word “wait” twice in this verse, and then a third time in the next verse. All this was in hope of God's promise that He would rescue him from all his afflictions. For God's word confirms to him God's care and help; therefore he was reassured, and even his love and faith in God grew, for the affliction pushed him a step forward in his attachment to God.

130.4.0.en: My soul waits for the Lord more than they that watch for the morning; I say, more than they that watch for the morning.

130.4.1.en: 1- David waits for the Lord with longing and concern more than the night watchman who waits for the dawn to break.

130.4.2.en: He confirms his longing by repeating the phrase twice in this same verse, and this signifies the difficulty of patience throughout the night, and the increase of longing to see the light of dawn. So everyone who passes through affliction, or wants to be rid of sin, awaits this hope with intense longing.

130.4.3.en: 2- The Jews used to set guards for the temple who watched in the night for the dawn to break, and waited for it with great concern, so that when they saw the dawn they hastened to offer the morning sacrifice, which is the burnt offering. So David's waiting for the Lord is with intense longing to offer Him holy worship, thanksgiving and praise.

130.4.4.en: 3- The waiting for the dawn that David awaited signifies, in the spirit of prophecy, the waiting for the Resurrection of Christ, which took place at the dawn of Sunday, to proclaim the salvation of all humanity that believes in Christ.

130.5.0.en: (Let Israel hope in the LORD; for with the LORD there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption. And He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.

130.5.1.en: Let hope: that is, let them hope.

130.5.2.en: 1- At the close of the psalm he calls the people of God who believe in Him, Israel, to place their hope in the Lord; for His mercies are many, or with Him is infinite mercy, and therefore He is ready to forgive them and support them, however great their sins and however hard their afflictions.

130.5.3.en: 2- God has redemption for His people from all their sins and their problems; His power is great and He has many means to save them. His redemption is complete to lift from them all their troubles; therefore let God's children be reassured, and hope in Him always.

130.5.4.en: 3- The redemption for which David and all the believers in the Old Testament hoped is the redemption of Christ, which was accomplished in the fullness of time, and it is the pledge of the complete redemption when Christ lifts them up to the Kingdom and compensates them for all their toils on the earth.

130.5.5.en: Look to God's mercy and His promises so that your heart may be strengthened, and depression may not strike you because of afflictions, or the sins into which you fall, but hasten to repentance and prayer, indeed to every good work, relying in this on God's mercy and His redemption.

130.5.6.en: Humility, striving and hope. A song of ascents. Of David. “LORD, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty) “.. v. 1. Introduction:

130.5.7.en: 1- Its writer: the prophet David, as the title of the psalm states.

130.5.10.en: a- When David went down to visit his brothers who were fighting the Philistines, and his eldest brother Eliab rebuked him, accusing him of pride, so he wrote this psalm, declaring his humility before God (1 Sam 17:28).

130.5.11.en: b- David wrote it when the servants of Saul accused him that he ought to seize the kingdom when he was a military commander, or one of the bravest commanders under Saul, to declare that he was not seeking this kingdom, although the prophet Samuel had anointed him king years before.

130.5.12.en: c- When Michal despised her husband David for his dancing before the ark of the covenant of God, he declared that he would make himself even smaller than this before the Lord (2 Sam 6:22).

130.5.13.en: 3- This psalm suits everyone who flees from the glory of the world, and humbles himself and hopes in God.

130.5.14.en: 4- Perhaps this psalm is a prophecy about the feelings of the captives in Babylon, or those returning from captivity, in humility before God, and they entreat Him to help them in building the temple and the acceptance of their worship.

130.5.15.en: 5- This psalm shows the feelings of the spiritual man who believes in God, so he humbles himself, and it exposes the sin of Satan the proud, who fell through his pride and his attempt to raise his throne and his position like God (Ezek 28:16-17). So also it rebukes the pride of the first man, Adam and Eve, who tried to become like God (Gen 3:5).

130.5.16.en: 6- This psalm is prayed on the twelfth step on the way of the ascent to the temple.

130.5.17.en: It is noticed that as one ascends and approaches the temple, one prays this psalm that calls to humility. The higher we rise toward God, the more humility we need, and the spiritual striving and hope in the Lord increase.

130.5.18.en: 7- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Compline, so that in it a person may declare his humility before God, hoping for his salvation after a whole day has passed, that He may forgive him all his sins and give him quiet sleep and a place in eternity.

131.0.0.en: LORD, my heart is not haughty, nor my eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.

131.0.1.en: Lofty: not exalted and not proud.

131.0.2.en: 1- David declares that he did not fall into pride in his feelings, and did not look with his eye to the kingdom, or a position higher than the one he was in; not in order to boast of his humility, but to thank God for the grace of humility that He gave him, whether in his heart, or in the look of his eyes, or in his conduct and works.

131.0.3.en: 2- David did not desire to sit on the throne and remove Saul, although he had been anointed by the hand of Samuel, and God had rejected Saul because of his sins, but he remained subject to Saul. Indeed, when Saul fell into David's hand twice, he said how could he stretch out his hand against the Lord's anointed (1 Sam 24:6), and he did not kill him, although Saul tried many times to kill David.

131.0.4.en: 3- Here David resembles Christ in his humility, for David is a type of Christ, and therefore God blessed David when He said of him, “I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after My own heart” (Acts 13:22).

132.0.s.en: (1) David desires to build the house of the Lord

132.0.0.en: LORD, remember David, and all his afflictions: how he swore unto the LORD, and vowed unto the mighty God of Jacob:

132.0.1.en: The mighty God of Jacob: that is, the great God, the God of Jacob.

132.0.2.en: 1- David entreats God to remember his humility and weakness, for he declares that he is nothing before God, that He may have compassion on him and bless him.

132.0.3.en: 2- If the writer is Solomon, he reminds God that He has fulfilled what He promised his father David, who humbled himself before God and vowed to build a house for Him. And that You, O God, said to him that your son Solomon is the one who will build the house, and I have built it; so bless it, and bless everyone who enters it to worship.

132.0.4.en: 3- David also shows his love in his oath and his vow to God that he would build a house for Him, because David was living in a great house made of cedar wood, while God dwelt in a tent; this shows David's love for God, although he had no power to build the house without God's permission. God did not permit David to build it, but David is the first to declare his love for God in his desire to build for Him a great house in place of the moving tent.

132.1.0.en: “Surely I will not come into the tabernacle of my house, nor go up into my bed; I will not give sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids,

132.1.2.en: 1- David spent all his effort to find a dwelling for the Lord and to build Him a house; he did not rest from searching and preparing the building materials all day, and also at night he did not tire of praying that God would fulfill his longings and permit the building of the house. He gave his body no rest to achieve his goal.

132.1.3.en: 2- David worked with perseverance to build the house, because Satan opposes the works of God and searches for a gap through which to enter, and David gave him no opportunity by continuing in striving and prayer. David represents seriousness in work, and once he has begun he must complete it.

132.2.0.en: Until I find out a place for the LORD, an habitation for the mighty God of Jacob.”

132.2.2.en: David wanted to find a place, a dwelling and a rest for the Lord, who in his sight is more important than any man. How could David rest in his house and his palace while God has no place of His own? By “place” he means a great place suited to the glory of God. He did not say “I will build Him a house,” because he knows that God is the Builder, and David longs only that there be a place in which God is pleased to dwell.

132.3.0.en: Lo, we heard of it at Ephratah; we found it in the fields of the wood.

132.3.1.en: Ephratah: a Hebrew word meaning fruitful, and it is Bethlehem, which lies southwest of Jerusalem at a distance of 8 km.

132.3.2.en: Fields of the wood: the wood means wilderness places, or places of forests. What is meant here is the village of Jearim, which lies southwest of Jerusalem at a distance of 18 km. The word Jearim means forests.

132.3.3.en: 1- David heard that the ark was in the region of Ephratah, so he searched for it until he found it in the village of Jearim, in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, and he moved it with great celebration to Jerusalem (2 Chr 1:4). This shows David's diligence and seriousness in searching for the ark of the covenant of God because of his heart's attachment to God; for the ark of the covenant represents the presence of God.

132.3.4.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about the Incarnation of Christ, who was born in Bethlehem, which is Ephratah (Gen 35:19), and He came to save the whole world; for the fields of the wood signify the Gentiles. He was born of the tribe of Judah in Bethlehem, but He also came to save all humanity.

132.4.0.en: “We will go into His tabernacles; we will worship at His footstool.”

132.4.1.en: 1- When David found the ark of the covenant he moved it with great celebration to Jerusalem, and called all the people to worship before it, that is, to submit to His commandments and His Law, and to surrender life to Him. This shows David's submission to God and acceptance of His will in all his life.

132.4.2.en: 2- This worship in Ephratah happened with Christ, born in the manger, by the shepherds, and then by the Magi. And God's footstool signifies His Incarnation.

132.4.3.en: Weary your body in spiritual striving and in fulfilling your responsibilities, and your spirit will rest; for the more the body is pressed, the stronger the spirit becomes, and then God is pleased to dwell in it, and this is God's dwelling, and the greatest place He seeks, that is, your heart, that He may reign over it and satisfy you with His love.

132.5.s.en: (2) Bringing back the ark of the covenant

132.5.0.en: Arise, O LORD, into Your rest; You, and the ark of Your strength.

132.5.1.en: 1- David calls on God to arise from Jearim, that is, the ark of the covenant of God, and be moved to Jerusalem to settle there, for he knows that God is the mover of the whole world, and He permitted Himself to be among His people by means of His ark of the covenant. Therefore he says to Him, arise and move, and his heart is full of joy that God will dwell in Jerusalem beside him, or more precisely, David will be beside God who dwells in Jerusalem. And David feels that the ark of God's strength is the ark of pride and glory, because God is above all gods.

132.5.2.en: 2- Moses used to repeat this verse when the ark journeyed in the wilderness of Sinai (Num 10:35-36), and Solomon also said it after building the temple at its dedication (2 Chr 6:41-42).

132.5.3.en: 3- This verse applies to the captives returning to Jerusalem, whose feelings repeated this verse after the rebuilding of the temple.

132.5.4.en: 4- In the spirit of prophecy David calls Christ to arise from the bosom of the Father and condescend and become incarnate for the redemption of His people. And he also calls Him, while He is in the tomb after His death on the Cross, to rise from the dead, declaring His victory over death for the benefit of His people, to give resurrection to everyone who believes in Him.

132.5.5.en: 5- The rest of the Lord is also the Church, in which God arises and dwells in the midst of His people, and the ark of strength is also the womb of the Virgin from which Christ was born.

132.6.0.en: Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your saints shout for joy.

132.6.1.en: Since the ark has settled in Jerusalem, the psalmist calls on the priests to live in righteousness and purity, so that they may stand before God to serve Him. As for His people, let them be in great joy, and praise God with continual shouting and glorification. This is fulfilled, in the spirit of prophecy, more clearly in the Church of the New Testament.

132.6.2.en: May you, my brother, call on God, whose Holy Spirit dwelling in you you have neglected, to arise and be kindled within you, and may you give Him a greater place in your life and hold fast to His commandments, so that He always finds His rest in you and works freely in all your thoughts and words and deeds.

132.7.s.en: (3) The promise to the offspring of David

132.7.0.en: For Your servant David's sake turn not away the face of Your anointed.

132.7.1.en: 1- The prophet David says in the spirit of prophecy, entreating God, who promised to set his son Solomon as king after him and that he would build a temple for the Lord, and David asks Him not to turn away the face of His anointed, that is, Solomon, anointed king, and to help him build a temple for Him.

132.7.2.en: 2- If the writer of the psalm is Solomon, he entreats God, interceding by his father David, who had died by then, that He not turn away the face of His anointed, that is, Solomon himself, and bless him to build and dedicate the temple. And this verse is found with the same text in Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple (2 Chr 6:42).

132.8.0.en: The LORD has sworn in truth unto David; He will not turn from it: “Of the fruit of your body will I set upon your throne. If your children will keep My covenant and My testimony that I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon your throne for evermore.”

132.8.1.en: 1- These two verses are God's promise to David that He will put his offspring on the throne of David, that is, the throne of the kingdom of Judah, for ever (2 Sam 7:12-13). And indeed this was fulfilled until the Babylonian captivity, and was completed in Christ, who comes of the offspring of David, to reign for ever.

132.8.2.en: 2- The condition for the offspring of David to sit on his throne for ever is their keeping God's covenant and His testimonies. Some of this offspring lived in righteousness and the worship of God, and some did not keep His commandments, and therefore God permitted the captivity as a punishment for them. And when they returned to repentance before God, God's promise was renewed in Christ, incarnate in the fullness of time. So the angel declared to the Virgin that the Lord would give the One born of her the throne of His father David (Lk 1:31); Christ sat on the throne of His father David, and He will continue to reign over the hearts of those who believe in Him for ever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

132.8.3.en: Ask the intercession of the saints and God will have mercy on you, as Solomon interceded by David his father (v. 10), because intercession is precious to God, for it declares your love for His children, and your longing for God, and your humility before Him, and so He grants you abundant blessings.

132.9.0.en: For the LORD has chosen Zion; He has desired it for His habitation: “This is My rest for ever; here will I dwell, for I have desired it.

132.9.1.en: 1- God chose Zion, that is, Jerusalem, because His temple is in it, and He found rest in its being His dwelling.

132.9.2.en: And God's rest is in the prayers of His children and their praises lifted up to Him, for He rejoices in the faith of His children and His love for them.

132.9.3.en: 2- He says that His rest is in Jerusalem for ever, and of course He does not mean the city of Jerusalem in Judea, because it was destroyed in AD 70 by the hand of Titus the Roman. But He means the Jerusalem that is the Church of the New Testament, which extends for ever into the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

132.9.4.en: 3- The writer of the psalm called on the Lord and said to Him, “Arise, O LORD, into Your rest” (v. 8), and the Lord answers in (v. 14) and says that My rest is in Jerusalem, that is, in the prayers of My children and their praises.

132.9.5.en: 4- Jerusalem is the soul that believes in God, in the Old Testament and the New Testament, and He rests in it for ever, because this soul is immortal with Him in the Kingdom.

132.10.0.en: I will abundantly bless her provision; I will satisfy her poor with bread.

132.10.1.en: 1- As long as God dwells in the midst of His people, He blesses their material needs and satisfies all the poor in it, so that all are content materially and thank God.

132.10.2.en: 2- Christ in His Church satisfies His poor children in spirit, that is, the humble, and gives them their spiritual needs, in addition to the material, and gives them above all His Body and Blood.

132.10.3.en: 3- The food of the Church (or her catch in the Septuagint translation) is her children and those who join her and believe in Christ; He blesses them and satisfies them spiritually and materially.

132.11.0.en: I will also clothe her priests with salvation, and her saints shall shout aloud for joy.

132.11.1.en: 1- God gives a special blessing to His children the priests, because they serve in His temple and lead His people in the spiritual way, so He grants them salvation, that is, deliverance from sins and the preoccupations of the world, that they may enjoy fellowship with God. As for all the godly believers, they praise God, and even shout with all their hearts, rejoicing. These blessings for the godly priests He gives them in the Old Testament, and all the more in the New Testament from the abundant blessings of the Holy Spirit.

132.11.2.en: 2- In the ninth verse the writer of the psalm calls on the Lord and asks Him to clothe the priests with righteousness and make the godly shout for joy. And God answers in (v. 16), responding to the call of the writer of the psalm, and confirms that He will clothe the priests with salvation and make the godly shout aloud.

132.12.0.en: There will I make the horn of David to bud; I have ordained a lamp for My anointed. His enemies will I clothe with shame, but upon himself shall his crown flourish.”

132.12.1.en: 1- The horn of David that God makes to bud is Christ, who comes of the offspring of David. And “I have ordained a lamp for My anointed”

132.12.2.en: what is meant by it is David's prophecy about Christ, in addition to the prophecies of the prophets, such as Isaiah and Jeremiah ...

132.12.3.en: Then John the Baptist, the forerunner of Christ, who prepared the way for Him.

132.12.4.en: 2- The ordaining of the lamp for Christ is the Body of Christ that He took from the Virgin, because Christ is the light of the world. And by the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption, shame came upon the enemies of Christ, that is, the demons. And the flourishing crown of Christ is the Church, and the head of this flourishing crown is Christ.

132.12.5.en: 3- Christ, who is the lamp of the world, a light whose divinity appeared through His life on the earth, through His words and His miracles, and His holiness appeared in that He did not sin, and His holiness and His light appeared still more in His Transfiguration on the mountain, and then in His Resurrection and Ascension.

132.12.6.en: 4- Although the psalm began with humiliation in (v. 1), it ends with glory and light and holiness in Christ who comes of the offspring of David, who enlightens the whole world and all who believe in Him.

132.12.7.en: God wants to enlighten your life, so He drives all the darkness of sin from you when you repent and adorns you with virtues, so that you are a light to the world and the salt of the earth, and He supports you in your spiritual striving until you reach the glories of heaven.

132.12.8.en: Brotherly love. A song of ascents. Of David. “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together” (v. 1). Introduction:

132.12.9.en: 1- Its writer: the prophet David, as appears from the title of the psalm.

132.12.10.en: 2- When was it written? After David became king over all the children of Israel, to call them to love and brotherhood in their worship of God.

132.12.11.en: 3- This psalm is a prophecy about the feelings of the Jews returning from captivity with joy, to dwell together in Jerusalem and Judea and build the temple, to worship God in it with one heart.

132.12.12.en: 4- This psalm is liturgical, because it was chanted at the three great feasts of the Jews, which are the Passover, Pentecost and Tabernacles, in which all the males of the children of Israel come before the temple of God to worship Him, and bring their families with them.

132.12.13.en: 5- This psalm declares the importance of brotherly love and of brethren dwelling together, so it is fitting for every believer to chant it in the midst of the Church in every spiritual atmosphere, or in a setting where the believers gather.

132.12.14.en: 6- This psalm declares the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church among the brethren who are members of the one body and are bound by love and unity. If the previous psalm tells us of the saving work of Christ and His rest in His Church, this psalm declares the work of the Holy Spirit in the salvation which He pours out on the Church.

132.12.15.en: 7- This psalm used to be prayed on the fourteenth of the steps of the ascent to the temple of the Lord.

132.12.16.en: 8- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Compline, to remind the believers of the importance of brotherly love among them, so that if there are any differences, or distress in hearts, they give them up and forgive one another, so that they find rest in the hands of God.
